headline: Hot CPI and an AI-debt rout hit tech; futures lean lower into PPI and retail sales
summary: September CPI ran hotter than forecast (3.7% year over year vs. 3.6% expected), and the S&P 500 fell 1.1% and the Nasdaq 1.9% as chip and AI-infrastructure names sold off for a seventh straight session. The Nikkei fell nearly 5% overnight and Europe slid, so Nasdaq 100 futures are down about 1.3% while S&P futures are off about 0.3%. Energy, health care and staples are holding up best, so today's tape favors patience in extended tech and attention to the 8:30 AM ET PPI and retail sales prints.

fed.note: Raised 25 bp in September; hot CPI keeps another hike on the table, though a hold is still the base case.

drivers.title: Hot CPI revives rate-hike worries
drivers.body: September CPI rose 0.6% on the month and 3.7% from a year ago, with gasoline up about 7% on the month. Core was 0.3% on the month and 2.6% year over year, a touch above forecasts. The 10-year yield sits near 5.2%, which pressures valuations and rate-sensitive groups.

drivers.title: AI and chip complex under pressure
drivers.body: Semiconductors fell for a seventh straight session, the Nasdaq had its worst day since July, and overnight the Nikkei dropped nearly 5% with European chipmakers sharply lower. Worries about data-center debt and financing costs (CoreWeave is the focal point) are overriding TSMC's record profit.

drivers.title: Banks stumble on earnings
drivers.body: Big-bank results were mixed: Goldman beat on trading but Wells Fargo fell, and Bank of America had its worst day in 18 months. Financials are down about 6% over the past month, with only 17% of the sector above its 50-day average.

drivers.title: Oil stays high but headline-driven
drivers.body: Brent is near $104 and WTI near $94, supported by a record pace of tanker attacks near Hormuz, while reports that the US may ease shipping sanctions pushed prices lower overnight. Energy leaders keep making highs even as crude is down about 8% over the past month.

drivers.title: Defensives and health care catch a bid
drivers.body: Money rotated into defensives as inflation data hit tech: Walmart rose about 3% and a health-care rally lifted Lilly, Merck and AbbVie (AbbVie at an all-time high), helped by UnitedHealth's raised outlook. Health care and staples are the sectors with the best breadth outside energy.

drivers.title: Breadth is thin beneath the index
drivers.body: Only 36% of S&P 500 stocks are above their 50-day average and 26% of the MidCap 400, with the Russell 2000 down about 5% in a month. Leadership is narrow: energy, health care, steel, software and a few staples.

risks.title: Inflation keeps the Fed in hiking mode
risks.body: CPI came in hot and energy prices are pushing headline inflation higher. A hot PPI today or another firm print would raise odds of a hike on Oct 28.

risks.title: AI-debt contagion
risks.body: CoreWeave's slide and data-center debt worries are spreading to chips, storage and servers. Failure to stabilize could drag the Nasdaq and the index further.

risks.title: Oil whipsaw around Hormuz
risks.body: Tanker attacks are at record pace but sanctions easing is under discussion. A deal could drop crude and energy leaders quickly; escalation would lift inflation fears.

risks.title: Long-end yields near 5%
risks.body: The 10-year is near 5.2% with deficit concerns in focus. Higher yields hurt valuations, housing and real estate.

risks.title: Thin breadth
risks.body: Only 36% of S&P 500 stocks are above their 50-day average, so index drawdowns can accelerate when the few leaders slip.

avoid.name: Homebuilders
avoid.detail: Homebuilding has 0% of names above their 200-day average and ITB is down about 16% over three months with the 10-year near 5.2%.

avoid.name: Aerospace & defense
avoid.detail: ITA is down about 11% over three months and GE, RTX, LMT and BA all sit well below their 50-day averages.

avoid.name: Airlines
avoid.detail: JETS is down about 17% over three months, with jet fuel costs up and only 20% of the industry above its 200-day average.

avoid.name: Banks and regional banks
avoid.detail: KBE and KRE are each down about 11-12% over three months and Bank of America had its worst day in 18 months.

avoid.name: Solar
avoid.detail: TAN is down about 21% over three months and 22% below its 200-day average.

avoid.name: REITs
avoid.detail: Only 10% of real estate names are above their 50-day average and the sector is down about 12% over three months.

avoid.name: Large-cap software laggards
avoid.detail: Oracle sits about 58% below its high, with Adobe and IBM also well below trend while newer software leaders hold up.

sectors.name: Energy
sectors.note: Strongest group in the scan, with 71% of names above their 200-day and refiners and E&Ps near highs. Extended names like VLO and XOM favor buying dips; a sanctions-easing deal that drops crude is the main risk.

sectors.name: Health Care
sectors.note: Rallied on UnitedHealth's beat-and-raise and sector-wide strength, with life-science tools and managed care among the best industries. A defensive group with real earnings support.

sectors.name: Consumer Staples
sectors.note: Beverage and tobacco leaders are at highs as investors rotate to defensives. Packaged foods remain weak, so favor beverages over food.

sectors.name: Information Technology
sectors.note: Software and cybersecurity are still in uptrends while hardware, storage and semiconductors are sliding on AI-debt worries and analyst downgrades of Dell and NetApp. Prefer software leaders over the chip complex until semis stabilize.

sectors.name: Utilities
sectors.note: Defensive bid helps and Southern Company is firm today, but only 28% of the group is above its 200-day average and rising yields cap the upside.

sectors.name: Materials
sectors.note: Steel is among the strongest industries while construction materials are the weakest. The sector is mixed with weak breadth, so be selective.

sectors.name: Financials
sectors.note: Bank earnings disappointed and the sector is down about 6% in a month with weak breadth. Insurers and reinsurers (MET, RGA, TRV) are the pockets of relative strength.

sectors.name: Communication Services
sectors.note: The sector is down about 5% in a month with weak breadth, but Meta holds a leader setup ahead of its Oct 21 earnings. Event risk is high.

sectors.name: Industrials
sectors.note: Only 18% of names are above their 50-day average and aerospace and defense is in a clear downtrend. A few distributors and logistics names hold up, but there is no broad trend to lean on.

sectors.name: Real Estate
sectors.note: Only 10% of names are above their 50-day average and the group is down about 12% over three months with the 10-year near 5.2%. Hotel REITs are the lone relative strength.

sectors.name: Consumer Discretionary
sectors.note: Homebuilders, airlines, auto retail and leisure are in downtrends, and energy-driven inflation squeezes consumers. A few apparel and appliance names are leading against the group.

picks.name: APA Corporation
picks.thesis: Crude is still historically high and E&Ps are the cleanest way to own it with a trend intact. A fall in crude on a sanctions-easing deal would undercut the setup.

picks.name: Permian Resources
picks.thesis: A Permian producer in a leader setup with analysts above the price and the oil complex still strong. A break of the risk line or a sharp oil drop would invalidate it.

picks.name: AbbVie
picks.thesis: At an all-time high as health care rallies on the UnitedHealth read-through and a defensive bid. A close back below the risk line would break the trend.

picks.name: Humana
picks.thesis: UnitedHealth's beat and raised outlook is a read-through for managed care, and the stock holds a leader setup. Medical-cost surprises at its Nov 6 report are the risk.

picks.name: Charles River Laboratories
picks.thesis: Life-science tools are among the best industries, and a JPMorgan target raise supports the move. Falling below the risk line would invalidate it.

picks.name: Coca-Cola Company (The)
picks.thesis: Defensive rotation is pushing beverages to highs as inflation hits growth stocks. Rising yields or a swift return to risk-on would cool the bid.

picks.name: Microsoft
picks.thesis: The cleanest large-cap tech leader, with analysts raising targets on Azure strength while chips and AI-debt names sell off. Earnings on Oct 28 is the next test.

picks.name: Docusign
picks.thesis: Software has held up better than hardware and Docusign hit a 52-week high on new product launches and an expanded Salesforce partnership. A high-multiple name, so a rates spike is the risk.

picks.name: MetLife
picks.thesis: Life insurers are holding up while banks stumble, and higher yields help investment income. A broader financials breakdown is the risk.

picks.name: Reinsurance Group of America
picks.thesis: Reinsurance is one of the strongest industries and RGA is at its high. Sharp market-wide de-risking would test it.

picks.name: Nucor
picks.thesis: Steel is the second-strongest industry in the scan and analysts are constructive. Oct 26 earnings and any softening in demand are the swing factors.

picks.name: Abercrombie & Fitch
picks.thesis: A standout in a weak consumer group with strong relative strength. A weak retail sales print or consumer squeeze from energy prices would be the invalidation.

picks.name: Meta Platforms
picks.thesis: A leader setup in a weak sector with earnings on Oct 21. Event risk is high, so size accordingly.

picks.name: NorthWestern Energy
picks.thesis: A defensive utility in a leader setup as investors seek safety. Another leg higher in yields would pressure the group.

picks.name: Valero Energy
picks.thesis: Refiners are the strongest industry and Valero set an all-time high this week, but the stock is far above its 50-day average. Better bought on a pullback toward that average.

picks.name: ExxonMobil
picks.thesis: Hit an all-time high on Wednesday with crude supported by Hormuz disruption, but it is extended and RSI is elevated. Wait for a dip rather than chasing.

picks.name: Dynatrace
picks.thesis: A software leader in a strong group, but it is well above its 50-day average. Better entry on a pullback ahead of Nov 4 earnings.
